title: Tasked chapter manifest
description: One chapter folder's chapter.json, under config/tasked/quests/. The folder it sits in must be named after the chapter's id, and `quests` lists the file names of that chapter's quests, in the order they should appear.

$schema.description: Ignored by Tasked. For your editor. Depth-counted: three levels up from a chapter folder is the quest root.

id.description: Must equal the name of the folder this file is in. Tasked reports the mismatch naming both sides, and uses the folder name.

description.description: Paragraphs. A bare string is also accepted, for a one-line description.

progressionMode.description: In a linear chapter the order of the `quests` list *is* the progression: each unlocks when the one above it completes, and no dependsOn is needed. A linear chapter that also declares dependsOn is a warning, not an error - the explicit edges win and the list order is then doing nothing.

defaultPrerequisiteMode.description: What every quest in this chapter uses unless it says otherwise.

defaultConsumeItems.description: Whether item tasks in this chapter take the items unless the task says otherwise. The inherited default, which is why it lives here: an author sets it once for a whole trade chapter.

theme.description: A palette this chapter asks to be drawn in. A client concept: the catalogue of themes lives on the client, so this is a plain string here and is reported by the client that could not resolve it.

quests.description: The file names of this chapter's quests, in order. Load-bearing rather than cosmetic: a LINEAR chapter's progression *is* this order. A name here that is not on disk is reported; a quest file that is not named here is reported and never loads.

text.description: Either a plain string, or a translation key with an English fallback.

fallback.description: Shown if the translation is missing. Without it a player sees the raw key.

itemRef.description: An item and a count. Not an ItemStack - resolved at the moment it is used.

item.description: Namespaced item id, e.g. minecraft:oak_log. A missing mod is an error, not a warning: the quest could never be completed.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. This id appears in player progress files, so changing it needs an entry in `aliases`.

name.description: A single path segment: the name of something in the same folder as the file that declares it. No separator, no `..`, and not beginning with `_` (every `_`-prefixed name is skipped, everywhere, so a reference to one could never resolve).
